subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is a hydrocarbon?
options: A compound containing only hydrogen and carbon
A compound containing hydrogen, carbon and oxygen
A compound containing only carbon atoms
A compound containing hydrogen and oxygen
questions.explain: A hydrocarbon is a compound made from hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.q: Which process is used to separate crude oil into useful fractions?
questions.explain: Fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions with similar boiling points.

questions.q: Alkanes are described as being:
questions.explain: Alkanes contain only single carbon-carbon bonds, so they are saturated.

questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n.

questions.q: Which monomer is used to make poly(ethene)?
questions.explain: Many ethene monomers join together by addition polymerisation to form poly(ethene).

questions.q: What is the approximate size range of nanoparticles?
questions.explain: Nanoparticles are extremely small, typically ranging from about 1 to 100 nanometres.

questions.q: Which of the following is a use of nanoparticles?
options: As a building material for bridges
As a fuel in car engines
questions.explain: Nanoparticles are used in sunscreens because they block ultraviolet light effectively.

questions.q: Why do hydrocarbons with larger molecules have higher boiling points?
options: They have stronger intermolecular forces that need more energy to overcome
questions.explain: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces, so more energy is needed to separate them.

questions.q: In a fractional distillation column, where does the fraction with the smallest molecules leave?
options: Near the top, where it is coolest
Near the bottom, where it is hottest
In the middle of the column
It does not leave the column
questions.explain: Small molecules have low boiling points, so they condense and leave near the cool top of the column.

questions.q: What are the products of the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon?
questions.explain: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in plenty of oxygen produces carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Which toxic gas is produced during the incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon?
questions.explain: Incomplete combustion, in a limited supply of oxygen, produces poisonous carbon monoxide.

questions.q: What is produced when a large alkane molecule is cracked?
questions.explain: Cracking breaks large alkanes into smaller, more useful alkanes and alkenes.

questions.q: How many products are formed when alkene monomers undergo addition polymerisation?
questions.explain: In addition polymerisation the monomers join to form only a single product, the polymer.

questions.q: Which feature of a monomer allows it to take part in addition polymerisation?
questions.explain: The C=C double bond opens up, allowing the monomers to join together in addition polymerisation.

questions.q: What happens to the surface area to volume ratio of a particle as its size decreases?
questions.explain: As particles get smaller their surface area to volume ratio increases, which makes nanoparticles very useful.

questions.q: An alkane molecule contains three carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula?
questions.explain: Using CnH2n+2 with n = 3 gives (2 x 3) + 2 = 8 hydrogens, so C3H8.

questions.q: Cracking C10H22 produces octane, C8H18, and one other molecule. What is it?
questions.explain: To balance atoms, C10H22 becomes C8H18 plus C2H4 (ethene), since 8+2 carbons and 18+4 hydrogens match.

questions.q: A student adds bromine water to an unknown hydrocarbon and it turns from orange to colourless. What does this show?
questions.explain: Alkenes decolourise bromine water because of their reactive C=C double bond, unlike alkanes.

questions.q: The monomer chloroethene undergoes addition polymerisation. What is the name of the polymer produced?
questions.explain: Addition polymers are named by putting the monomer name in brackets after poly, giving poly(chloroethene).
